name: Drain
label: Revelation
lede: A Santa Cruz band in board shorts made a thrash-crossover record for Revelation, watched the pandemic cancel the tour, then threw a parking-lot show in San Jose that helped kick off a hardcore boom.

eras.title: College kids turn into a fight band
eras.text: Drain started as drummer Tim Flegal and a group of UC Santa Cruz students trying out whatever styles they liked. When that line-up fell apart, Sammy Ciaramitaro and Cody Chavez steered it hard toward hardcore, with a lot of 1980s thrash in the riffs.

years.h: Tim Flegal starts Drain with UC Santa Cruz students
years.p: Drummer Tim Flegal forms Drain in Santa Cruz with Aric Gibson, Patrick Delaney and Josh Nunes, students at UC Santa Cruz playing in a mix of styles.

years.h: Sammy Ciaramitaro takes the mic and Drain goes hardcore
years.p: Singer Sammy Ciaramitaro and bassist Cody Chavez join as the first line-up breaks up, and Drain turns into a hardcore band. Demo '15 and Swan Songs follow.
years.xp:
Ciaramitaro grew up in an upper-middle-class Los Angeles suburb on gateway bands like [[The Offspring|23a03e33-a603-404e-bcbf-2c00159d7067]] before hardcore's storytelling pulled him in. He also drums in San Jose's Gulch, which he co-founded.

Chavez soon moved from bass to guitar, and Justin Rhode took over bass in 2016.

years.h: Drain's Over Thinking EP, and Sammy Ciaramitaro gets sober
years.p: Drain release the Over Thinking EP. Sammy Ciaramitaro told Stereogum he got sober in 2016.
Drain's second EP takes its name from the Twilight Zone episode.

eras.title: California Cursed, then locked down
eras.text: One set at Sound and Fury got Drain onto Revelation, and California Cursed came out in April 2020, just as touring stopped. When shows came back, Drain and their friends didn't wait for promoters.

years.h: Drain's Sound and Fury set lands them on Revelation
years.p: Drain's 2019 set at the Sound and Fury festival catches Revelation Records' attention, and the label signs them.
Ten songs in 22 minutes, announced in February with Sick One. It lands weeks into the COVID lockdown, and every tour date goes with it.
years.xp:
Sammy Ciaramitaro, Cody Chavez, Justin Rhode and Tim Flegal wrote it together and recorded it through 2019. Exclaim! gave it 8/10 and said it could carry you out of the dystopian nightmare and into the pit.

Stereogum's Tom Breihan called Drain old-school California fight music with a generous whiff of '80s thrash. Stuck at home, the band watched the record travel anyway.

years.h: Justin Rhode leaves; Mike Durrett takes Drain's bass
years.p: Justin Rhode, bassist on California Cursed, leaves in 2020 and Mike "Durt" Durrett takes over until 2022. On Living Proof, guitarist Cody Chavez also plays bass.

Stereogum reported that Sammy Ciaramitaro's girlfriend fell 15 feet through their rental's ceiling and broke her foot, followed by four months of the landlord leaving razors and glass outside and forging evidence.

q: We realized we could do this ourselves, that we don't need anybody else.
years.h: 2,000 people at Drain and Gulch's San Jose parking-lot show
years.p: Drain, Gulch, [[Scowl|c81f7820-ee5b-46ef-9b78-027d38b9a1aa]], [[Sunami|1b53aa11-ccef-457f-90d9-5165b270fdc5]], Xibalba and Maya Over Eyes play a self-built guerrilla show in a San Jose parking lot. About 2,000 come, some on plane tickets.
years.xp: The bands printed the merch and built the stage themselves. Stereogum later wrote that the show kicked off the national hardcore renaissance by accident, and the New York Times called Drain a driving force of it.

eras.title: Epitaph, and a borrowed cymbal
eras.text: Epitaph came for Drain, and Drain made them wait until California Cursed got its tour. The second album was cut partly at Dave Grohl's Studio 606 and ended with a Descendents cover sung clean.

years.h: Drain sign to Epitaph after months of talks
years.p: After six to eight months of negotiating, Drain leave Revelation for Epitaph Records, which agrees to let them tour California Cursed properly first. Watch You Burn is the first Epitaph single.

years.big: Taylor Hawkins' cymbal, on a hardcore record
years.h: Drain's Living Proof, made at Dave Grohl's Studio 606
years.p: Recording Living Proof at Studio 606, soon after Foo Fighters drummer Taylor Hawkins died, Tim Flegal broke his own cymbal and used one of Hawkins's instead.
years.xp:
The album closes with a clean-sung cover of [[Descendents|f035837e-4117-438d-a524-cacf43500e68]]' Good Good Things, and has a rap interlude and Grateful Dead nods throughout. Kerrang! gave it 5/5, and Revolver named it the best hardcore album of 2023.

Sammy Ciaramitaro, the self-described pessimist behind the scene's friendliest band, told Stereogum he reads the Descendents song as a conversation about trust between partners.

years.h: Drain headline North America, then Europe
years.p: Drain headline a US tour with rotating support from [[Drug Church|32d2897c-4c91-46db-8161-f51d3f4f0d93]], Gel and Magnitude, then headline Europe August 3–19, including Poland's Pol'and'Rock festival. Earlier that year they toured Australia with [[Comeback Kid|6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd]].

years.h: Revolver names Living Proof the best hardcore album of 2023
years.p: Revolver puts Drain's Living Proof at No. 1 among 2023's hardcore albums; Stereogum ranks it 47th of all albums that year and eighth in hardcore.

eras.title: Drain is your friend
eras.text: By their third album Drain were playing Warped Tour and metal festivals while Sammy Ciaramitaro still worked the merch table himself. The record was cut live to catch what they sound like in a room.

years.p: Drain announce their third album with the single Nights Like These. Sammy Ciaramitaro says they're still just friends who get to play music together.

years.h: Drain on Warped Tour and Louder Than Life
years.p: Drain play the revived Vans Warped Tour, plus Inkcarceration, Louder Than Life, New England Metal & Hardcore Festival and Furnace Fest.

q: I want to be the face everyone says hello to.
years.p: Drain's third album is recorded entirely live with producer Jon Markson (The Story So Far, Drug Church). Lead single Nights Like These gets a video by Derek Rathbun.
years.xp: Sammy Ciaramitaro still works the merch table at every show; he told Kerrang! he wants to be the face everyone says hello to. Off the road he's worked at Printhead, a San Jose T-shirt shop run by his former bandmate Cole Kakimoto.

years.p: Touring bassist Greg Cerwonka joins Drain full time, following Sam Jameson (2023–25). Through every bass change, Tim Flegal, Sammy Ciaramitaro and Cody Chavez have stayed put.
